stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
stimulus: Ornithologists once assumed that no land bird could cross the open Pacific in a single flight, since such birds cannot rest on water. Satellite tags fitted to shorebirds have since overturned that assumption. Departing from the mudflats of western Alaska each autumn, ______
choices: the journey of the bar-tailed godwit ends in New Zealand without a single stop.
the bar-tailed godwit reaches New Zealand without stopping once to feed or rest.
New Zealand is the destination the bar-tailed godwit reaches without stopping.
researchers have tracked bar-tailed godwits all the way to New Zealand nonstop.
explanation: The opening phrase 'Departing from the mudflats of western Alaska' describes whatever departs, and that is the bird. Choice B puts 'the bar-tailed godwit' right after the comma, so the modifier attaches to the right noun.

A.why: You let 'the bar-tailed godwit' inside the 'of' phrase count as the subject. The first noun is actually 'the journey', and a journey does not depart from mudflats. The bird does.

C.why: You looked for a sentence that mentions the bird. Here the first noun is 'New Zealand', so the sentence says New Zealand departs from Alaska, which is the reverse of what happens.

D.why: You picked the people connected to the event instead of the one doing the departing. 'Researchers' comes first, so the sentence says the researchers left the Alaskan mudflats each autumn.

stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
stimulus: Not every carbohydrate in a meal is broken down in the small intestine. Many plant fibers pass through it intact and are processed only later, farther along the digestive tract, where they turn out to play an important role in gut health. Fermented by bacteria in the large intestine, ______
choices: bacteria in the large intestine convert fiber into short-chain fatty acids for the colon.
the cells lining the colon are nourished by short-chain fatty acids made from fiber.
short-chain fatty acids are produced from fiber and then nourish the colon's lining.
dietary fiber yields short-chain fatty acids that nourish the cells lining the colon.
explanation: The thing 'fermented by bacteria' is the dietary fiber. Choice D begins with 'dietary fiber', so the opening phrase correctly describes the fiber.

A.why: You put the agent in place of the thing acted on. With 'bacteria' first, the sentence says the bacteria were fermented by bacteria, but the bacteria do the fermenting.

B.why: You chose the part of the body that benefits. 'The cells lining the colon' are not fermented by bacteria. They are fed by what the fermentation produces.

C.why: You chose the product instead of its source. The fatty acids come out of fermentation, so they are not the thing being fermented. The fiber is.

stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
stimulus: Economists have long debated whether loyalty to a single employer pays off over the course of a career. One study of payroll records followed nearly 30,000 employees across a decade and tracked every change of firm. Compared with peers who remained at a single firm for the full period, ______
choices: employees who changed firms at least twice saw their wages grow about 9 percent faster.
the wages of employees who changed firms at least twice grew about 9 percent faster.
changing firms at least twice was linked to wages that grew about 9 percent faster.
employers paid those who changed firms at least twice wages growing 9 percent faster.
explanation: The phrase 'Compared with peers who remained at a single firm' must be followed by people who can be compared with those peers. Choice A begins with 'employees who changed firms', so the comparison is between two groups of workers.

B.why: You let the 'of' phrase hide the real subject. The first noun is 'the wages', so the sentence compares wages with peers. That pairs a property with people instead of people with people.

C.why: You accepted an action as the subject. 'Changing firms' is a behavior, not a group of workers, so it cannot be compared with the peers who stayed.

D.why: You picked the other party in the job market. 'Employers' are not the group being compared with workers who stayed at one firm. The employees who switched are.

stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
stimulus: Most fossil plants are recovered as scattered leaves, seeds, and bark fragments, which makes it difficult to reconstruct an entire ecosystem. A coal-bearing site in northern China is a rare exception, where an eruption buried a swamp forest almost instantly. Preserved in volcanic ash for roughly 300 million years, ______
choices: paleobotanists have now mapped the ancient forest one tree at a time.
the eruption that buried the forest left each tree where it had grown.
the ancient forest still has its trees standing exactly where they grew.
the trees of the ancient forest still standing exactly where they grew.
explanation: The thing 'preserved in volcanic ash' is the ancient forest. Choice C begins with 'the ancient forest' and gives it a finite verb, 'has', so the result is a complete sentence with the modifier attached correctly.

A.why: You picked the people who study the forest. With 'paleobotanists' first, the sentence says the scientists were preserved in ash for 300 million years.

B.why: You picked the cause instead of the thing preserved. The eruption produced the ash, but the eruption was not preserved in it. The forest was.

D.why: You focused on the noun and missed the verb. 'Still standing' is an -ing form, not a conjugated verb, so the subject never gets a main verb and the sentence is a fragment.

stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
stimulus: Before 1995, most astronomers expected giant planets to orbit far from their stars, as Jupiter and Saturn do in our own solar system. The discovery of a planet around the Sun-like star 51 Pegasi upended that expectation almost overnight. Orbiting its host star once every 4.2 days, ______
choices: the star 51 Pegasi hosts a gas giant now described as a "hot Jupiter."
the planet 51 Pegasi b is a gas giant heated to roughly 1,000°C.
the surface of 51 Pegasi b is a gas layer heated to roughly 1,000°C.
astronomers classify 51 Pegasi b as a gas giant called a "hot Jupiter."
explanation: The thing 'orbiting its host star once every 4.2 days' is the planet. Choice B places 'the planet 51 Pegasi b' immediately after the comma, so the modifier describes the right object.

A.why: You picked the owner instead of the thing described. 'The star 51 Pegasi' comes first, so the sentence says the star orbits its own host star, which reverses the relationship.

C.why: You picked a feature of the planet instead of the planet itself. The surface does not orbit the star on its own. The whole planet does.

D.why: You picked the people who study the planet. With 'astronomers' first, the sentence says the astronomers orbit the star every 4.2 days.

stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
stimulus: Linguist Rahel Okafor spent three summers documenting Dovra, a language that has never had a written form. Spoken today by fewer than two hundred people in a handful of mountain villages, ______ a set of sounds that appear in no neighboring language.
choices: Okafor's recordings of Dovra preserve
Dovra's few remaining speakers use
the Dovra language contains
Okafor noted that Dovra had
explanation: The opening phrase, "Spoken today by fewer than two hundred people," describes something that people speak. That is the language. The noun right after the comma has to be the thing being described, so the clause must begin with "the Dovra language."

A.why: You let the subject become Okafor's recordings. Recordings are not spoken by two hundred villagers. The language is, so the opening phrase now describes the wrong thing.

B.why: You chose the people affected instead of the thing described. The speakers do the speaking. They are not "spoken by" anyone, so the modifier attaches to the wrong noun.

D.why: You let the first noun be Okafor. That makes the sentence say Okafor is spoken by two hundred villagers. Dovra shows up later in the clause, but only the first noun counts.

stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
stimulus: As sea levels rise along the coast of Bangladesh, salt water has crept into rice paddies that were once fresh. Plant breeders at a regional institute responded by crossing a traditional local rice with a high-yield strain. Bred to tolerate salty soil, ______ about 90 percent of the grain that standard rice produces on inland farms.
choices: the institute's researchers now harvest
coastal farmers are able to harvest
the new variety's harvest totals
the new variety reliably yields
explanation: Something was "bred to tolerate salty soil," and only a plant fits that description. The rice variety is what the breeders created, so "the new variety" has to come right after the comma.

A.why: You put the makers in place of the thing they made. The researchers did the breeding. They were not themselves bred to tolerate salt.

B.why: You chose the people who benefit instead of the plant. Farmers were not bred to tolerate salty soil.

C.why: You chose a property of the plant instead of the plant itself. The variety was bred to tolerate salt, not its harvest. The phrase "the new variety's" looks right, but the real subject here is "harvest."

stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
stimulus: Musicologist Ines Vallarta has spent a decade cataloging the surviving manuscripts of the eighteenth-century composer Teodora Ruiz. Composed for a court orchestra of only eleven players, ______ unusually spare scoring, with long passages written for just two violins.
choices: Vallarta has found that the symphonies have
Ruiz's symphonies consistently feature
Ruiz gave each of her symphonies
the eleven players performed works with
explanation: The thing "composed for a court orchestra" is a piece of music. When you ask what was composed, the answer is the symphonies, so "Ruiz's symphonies" has to be the subject that follows the comma.

A.why: You let the first noun be Vallarta, the scholar who studies the music. That makes the sentence say she was composed for a court orchestra. "The symphonies" comes too late in the clause to fix this.

C.why: You chose the artist instead of the artwork. Ruiz did the composing. She was not composed for an orchestra.

D.why: You chose the people who performed the music. The players were not composed for an orchestra. They made up the orchestra.

stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
stimulus: Each autumn, many ruby-throated hummingbirds fly nonstop across the Gulf of Mexico, a crossing of roughly 800 kilometers with nowhere to land. Weighing less than a nickel, ______ before setting out over open water.
choices: the hummingbird nearly doubles its mass by storing fat
the hummingbird's fat stores nearly double its mass
when the bird stores fat, its mass nearly doubles
ornithologists have recorded the bird doubling its mass
explanation: The thing that weighs less than a nickel is the bird. Choice A puts "the hummingbird" right after the comma, so the opening phrase describes the right thing.

B.why: You chose a part of the bird instead of the whole bird. The real subject is "fat stores," and the sentence is not saying the fat weighs less than a nickel. "Hummingbird's" is only a possessive and does not make the bird the subject.

C.why: Starting the clause with "when" moves the subject away from the phrase. The main subject becomes "its mass," and a mass does not weigh less than a nickel. The bird does.

D.why: You let the people observing the bird become the subject. That makes the sentence say the ornithologists weigh less than a nickel.

stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
stimulus: Ochre sea stars are top predators on rocky Pacific shores, where they keep mussel populations from crowding out other species. Guided by a simple eyespot at the tip of each arm, ______ toward shaded crevices as the tide goes out.
choices: biologists have watched the sea star crawl
the sea star's slow crawl carries it
the sea star slowly makes its way
the ebbing tide draws the sea star
explanation: The eyespots belong to the animal, and they guide the animal. Choice C puts "the sea star" right after the comma, so the opening phrase describes the right thing.

A.why: You let the people observing the animal become the subject. Biologists are not guided by an eyespot on each arm.

B.why: You chose something the animal does instead of the animal. The subject is "crawl," and a crawl does not have eyespots. "Sea star's" is only a possessive.

D.why: You chose a nearby force in the scene. The tide is not guided by eyespots, so putting it first makes the opening phrase describe the wrong thing.
